sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Repair the pre-1 July 2007 branch: do not unconditionally require firstScheduledDryDockingDate when the complete warning triangle and correctly positioned ice-class draught mark are already present. Encode the alternatives so a pre-cutoff applicable ship passes if the marking is already complete, or if a valid first scheduled dry-docking date strictly after 1 July 2007 is still future; once that date is due/past, require the complete marking, and treat a missing/invalid date as failure only when the marking is incomplete. Add sh:datatype xsd:date to firstScheduledDryDockingDate and preferably consolidate the three overlapping conditional SPARQL constraints into one bounded query while retaining the tolerance-based draught comparison.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The graph only requires a class certificate and six independent ship-owned draught values; it does not encode the required relationship that those values are indicated in that certificate. Locate the canonical indication/evidence relationship term and constrain the certificate evidence without moving or duplicating the draught properties from their authoritative ship owner. Also branch the marking rule by the 1 July 2007 construction-date cutoff: do not use one unconditional marking constraint for both cohorts, and for pre-cutoff ships encode the marking deadline relative to the first scheduled dry docking after 1 July 2007 rather than merely requiring a qualifying docking date alongside present-day marks.

Add the supplied nltl:iceClass applicability path on the ship with minCount 1, maxCount 1, and values in nltl:iceClassValue. Prevent accidental passes by requiring constructionDate, summerLoadLineFreshWaterDraught, and upperIceWaterlineDraught with Core minCount/maxCount constraints instead of only checking them when constructionDate happens to exist; remove that presence SPARQL. Add maxCount 1 to singular draught/mark paths and boolean flags, and require exactly one decimal numericValue and exactly one unit:M per quantity, so extra conflicting values cannot satisfy hasValue/EXISTS logic. Keep firstScheduledDryDockingDate conditional for pre-cutoff ships but constrain it to at most one date, then retain the cutoff logic and tolerant amidships comparison.
